annotations.description:
Annotations on the Bare Metal Node Pool.
This field has the same restrictions as Kubernetes annotations.
The total size of all keys and values combined is limited to 256k.
Key can have 2 segments: prefix (optional) and name (required),
separated by a slash (/).
Prefix must be a DNS subdomain.
Name must be 63 characters or less, begin and end with alphanumerics,
with dashes (-), underscores (_), dots (.), and alphanumerics between.


**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the annotations present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_annotations' for all of the annotations present on the resource.
annotations.rationale: annotations are not security related configurations.

bare_metal_cluster.description: The cluster this node pool belongs to.
bare_metal_cluster.rationale: Identifier referencing the parent cluster this node pool belongs to. We do not constrain references to other resources, so this is not a useful platform-policy target.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

display_name.description: The display name for the Bare Metal Node Pool.
display_name.rationale: display name does not impact the security of the resource.

location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

name.description: The bare metal node pool name.
name.rationale: name is not impact the security of the resource.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: project is not a security related configuration.

node_pool_config.labels.description:
The map of Kubernetes labels (key/value pairs) to be applied to
each node. These will added in addition to any default label(s)
that Kubernetes may apply to the node. In case of conflict in
label keys, the applied set may differ depending on the Kubernetes
version -- it's best to assume the behavior is undefined and
conflicts should be avoided. For more information, including usage
and the valid values, see:
  - http://kubernetes.io/v1.1/docs/user-guide/labels.html
An object containing a list of "key": value pairs.
For example: { "name": "wrench", "mass": "1.3kg", "count": "3" }.
node_pool_config.labels.rationale: labels are not security related configurations.

node_pool_config.operating_system.description: Specifies the nodes operating system (default: LINUX).
node_pool_config.operating_system.rationale: Selects the node OS family (default LINUX). It chooses the operating system, not a patch level/version, so the 'outdated OS' justification is incorrect; the OS family is a team operational choice with no single secure value to enforce.

node_pool_config.node_configs.description: The list of machine addresses in the Bare Metal Node Pool.

node_pool_config.node_configs.labels.description:
The map of Kubernetes labels (key/value pairs) to be applied to
each node. These will added in addition to any default label(s)
that Kubernetes may apply to the node. In case of conflict in
label keys, the applied set may differ depending on the Kubernetes
version -- it's best to assume the behavior is undefined and
conflicts should be avoided. For more information, including usage
and the valid values, see:
  - http://kubernetes.io/v1.1/docs/user-guide/labels.html
An object containing a list of "key": value pairs.
For example: { "name": "wrench", "mass": "1.3kg", "count": "3" }.

node_pool_config.node_configs.node_ip.description:
The default IPv4 address for SSH access and Kubernetes node.
Example: 192.168.0.1
node_pool_config.node_configs.node_ip.rationale: The IPv4 address assigned to a node for SSH/Kubernetes. It is an environment-specific address value; a platform policy cannot constrain it without hardcoding an IP, and the analogous IP fields on the cluster resources are treated as non-targets too.

node_pool_config.taints.description: The initial taints assigned to nodes of this node pool.

node_pool_config.taints.effect.description: Specifies the nodes operating system (default: LINUX). Possible values: ["EFFECT_UNSPECIFIED", "PREFER_NO_SCHEDULE", "NO_EXECUTE"]
node_pool_config.taints.effect.rationale: taints effect is not a security related configuration.

node_pool_config.taints.key.rationale: taints key is not a security related configuration.

node_pool_config.taints.value.rationale: taints value is not a security related configuration.
